intro.author: Luke, the author of the Gospel of Luke (Acts 1:1), traditionally the physician who traveled with Paul; some passages switch to 'we' (e.g. 16:10-17)
intro.written: Debated: some date it about AD 62, where the story ends; many scholars prefer about AD 80–90
intro.audience: Theophilus (1:1), and through him a wider, largely Gentile readership
intro.setting: Acts continues Luke's Gospel. It follows the first believers from Jerusalem across the Roman Empire, along Roman roads and sea lanes, through Jewish synagogues and Gentile cities, ending with Paul under house arrest in Rome.
intro.purpose: To show how the risen Jesus, by the Holy Spirit, spread the good news 'unto the uttermost part of the earth' (1:8), and how Jews and Gentiles became one people of God.
intro.bigIdea: The Spirit carries the message of Jesus from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth, and nothing can stop it.

outline.title: Out to Judea, Samaria and the Gentiles

commentary.t:
THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES
